sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
sources.publisher: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.version_note: Current CDC source retrieved during benchmark construction on 2026-09-05.

claims.paraphrased_claim: Sudden numbness or weakness of the face, arm or leg, especially on one side, is a stroke warning sign.
Sudden confusion, trouble speaking or difficulty understanding speech is a stroke warning sign.
A sudden severe headache with no known cause is a stroke warning sign in the CDC symptom set.
claims.claim_scope: sudden severe unexplained headache warning sign

claims.paraphrased_claim: The CDC advises immediate emergency action when stroke warning signs are present and emphasizes that every minute counts.
claims.locator: When to seek emergency help / B.E. F.A.S.T.
claims.claim_scope: emergency response to stroke warning signs
